documents.title: Standard for Acceptable Use of Artificial Intelligence with University Data
documents.summary: An IT standard for all JMU faculty, staff and students on using AI with university data. It names Copilot Chat as the only approved GenAI tool, requires review for others, sets data-protection and disclosure duties, and lists risks. It does not set classroom rules and points to separate AI in Education guidance.
documents.stance_why: The standard says Copilot Chat 'is the only GenAI tool currently approved for use by the entire JMU community' and that other tools need IT approval, so AI tools are restricted to an approved one unless reviewed, while it also 'supports responsible use and experimentation'. It does not hand the decision to instructors, so restrict.

units.why: The Purpose sets the standard's scope: 'requirements for all JMU users' on 'acceptable and ethical use of AI', so it is an institution-wide framework (P56), not a rule on classwork.
units.anchor: requirements for all JMU users (faculty, staff, & students) on the acceptable and ethical use

units.why: The scope sentence says the standard covers 'stand-alone, embedded, and generative AI within other systems or applications'; this defines what the policy covers (P61). It touches embedded AI (P07) but states scope, not a rule for editors or agents.
units.anchor: stand-alone, embedded, and generative AI within other systems or applications
units.frag_start: This standard applies to: both existing

units.why: The Definitions section defines 'Artificial Intelligence (AI)' as 'the simulation of human intelligence processes by machines', which sets what the policy covers (P61).
units.anchor: The simulation of human intelligence processes by machines, especially computer systems

units.why: The definition of 'Generative Artificial Intelligence' as a type of AI that generates 'new content, such as text images, and audio' fixes the scope of GenAI rules (P61).
units.anchor: A type of artificial intelligence that can learn from and mimic large amounts of data

units.why: The definition of 'University Data' ('Data collected, maintained or used by university personnel...') sets what data the privacy rules protect; it is a scope definition, so P61.
units.anchor: Data collected, maintained or used by university personnel, contractors, or partners
units.frag_end: unless explicitly noted otherwise in writing

units.why: Names Copilot Chat as 'the only GenAI tool currently approved for use by the entire JMU community', a sanctioned, licensed tool and the only one allowed without review (P17; P50 fits the data side but the core is the sanctioned tool).
units.anchor: is the only GenAI tool currently approved for use by the entire JMU community

units.why: Explains that logged-in Copilot Chat users have 'data protections' and their data is not used 'to train the GenAI model'; a data-protection fact about the vetted tool, so P50.
units.anchor: users have data protections to ensure their access is not monitored
units.frag_start: Once logged into JMU-licensed Copilot Chat

units.why: Permits protected data including PII in Copilot Chat 'as necessary'; a conditional permission on data handling, so P50 (protect data, use vetted tools).
units.anchor: may be used in Microsoft Copilot Chat as necessary

units.why: 'Use of Highly Confidential Data in the JMU-licensed Copilot Chat is strictly prohibited' forbids a data type in AI; protecting confidential data is P50.
units.anchor: The use of Highly Confidential Data in the JMU-licensed Copilot Chat is strictly prohibited

units.why: Tools other than Copilot Chat 'must be submitted to IT for review and approval', a vetting requirement that restricts other AI tools; closest type is P50 (prefer vetted tools).
units.anchor: must be submitted to IT for review and approval through a Technology Solution Request

units.why: Bans DeepSeek on state devices and networks for 'faculty, staff, employees, affiliates, and contractors'; a named-tool ban. No type covers a banned named tool, and P50 (vetted tools) does not say the same, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: are prohibited from using DeepSeek AI Chatbot, or other tools developed by DeepSeek
units.uncovered_note: Named-tool ban (DeepSeek) on state-issued devices and networks under a state executive order.

units.why: 'JMU supports responsible use and experimentation with AI tools' states a welcoming institutional principle; closest is P56 (institution-wide framework) rather than P02 because it is not a default classroom permission.
units.anchor: James Madison University supports responsible use and experimentation with AI tools
units.frag_end: keep in mind when using these tools

units.why: 'Adhere to all laws and applicable University policies and standards' is a general compliance duty on all users, part of the institution-wide framework (P56).
units.anchor: Adhere to all laws and applicable University policies and standards.

units.why: 'Adhere to University guidance on AI in Education' ties users to the separate education guidance; it defers classroom rules elsewhere, so P56 (framework) rather than P04.
units.anchor: Adhere to University guidance on AI in Education.

units.why: 'Obtain IT review and approval for the use of AI tools other than Microsoft Copilot Chat' repeats the approval gate as a user duty; a distinct bullet in the Responsible Use list, coded P50 (vetted tools).
units.anchor: IT review and approval for the use of AI tools other than Microsoft Copilot Chat.

units.why: 'Use AI tools that have been appropriately contracted and licensed with the necessary data protections' requires vetted tools, P50.
units.anchor: Use AI tools that have been appropriately contracted and licensed with the necessary data

units.why: 'Do not share Highly Confidential Data (Class 1) or personally identifiable information (Class 2)' unless IT approves in writing; protecting personal data, P50.
units.anchor: Do not share Highly Confidential Data (Class 1) or personally identifiable information (Class 2) unless

units.why: The list names 'student/faculty/staff IDs, grades, financial information, intellectual property' as sensitive information not to be shared; kept as its own unit because it names grades and IP, coded P50.
units.anchor: student/faculty/staff IDs, grades, financial information, intellectual property, or other sensitive
units.frag_start: This includes, but is not limited to

units.why: 'Limit University Data in AI systems to only that which is necessary' is a data-minimization rule, P50.
units.anchor: Limit University Data in AI systems to only that which is necessary

units.why: 'Retain University Data in AI systems only for the length of time required' sets data retention limits, P50.
units.anchor: Retain University Data in AI systems only for the length of time required

units.why: 'Avoid sharing information that could compromise the privacy or security of anyone' is a privacy rule, P50.
units.anchor: Avoid sharing information that could compromise the privacy or security of anyone associated with

units.why: 'Avoid sharing information that could identify individual students or their data' is a student-privacy rule, P50.
units.anchor: Avoid sharing information that could identify individual students or their data.

units.why: 'Be cautious when seeking or providing information that could have legal, ethical, or reputational implications' is an ethics caution; closest is P53 (ethical concerns).
units.anchor: Be cautious when seeking or providing information that could have legal, ethical, or reputational implications.

units.why: 'Ensure all AI outputs are validated by a human(s) for bias and unintended consequences' requires human verification of output; P31 (verify AI output) fits better than P53 since the action is verification.
units.anchor: Ensure all AI outputs are validated by a human(s) for bias and unintended consequences.

units.why: 'Allow users the ability to consent to the use of their data by AI systems when possible' is a consent/privacy rule, P50.
units.anchor: Allow users the ability to consent to the use of their data by AI systems

units.why: Users must 'be transparent when generative AI or other AI related capabilities are utilized in any process or to produce any decision' using mandatory disclosures; a disclosure rule, P24.
units.anchor: Be transparent when generative AI or other AI related capabilities are utilized in any process

units.why: Requires the statement 'DISCLAIMER: This decision or output was generated by artificial intelligence' on AI-generated decisions or outputs; specific wording of disclosure, P24.
units.anchor: This decision or output was generated by artificial intelligence.
units.frag_start: The following disclosure, or a similar

units.why: Requires a different disclaimer, 'created with assistance from artificial intelligence', where AI assists but does not produce the final output; same disclosure duty with a distinct condition, P24.
units.anchor: This decision or output was created with assistance from artificial intelligence.
units.frag_start: The following disclaimer, or a similar

units.why: AI systems making external decisions about citizens 'shall disclose how AI is used', the extent of human involvement, and appeal options; a disclosure and appeal duty for decision systems, closest P24 since the core is disclosure.
units.anchor: disclose how AI is used to arrive at a decision

units.why: Under 'Understand the Risks', the standard says benefits and risks 'should be carefully evaluated to determine whether AI should be applied or prohibited'; a review-before-use principle at framework level, P56.
units.anchor: should be carefully evaluated to determine whether AI should be applied or prohibited
units.frag_start: The potential benefits and risks of AI

units.why: 'Not all AI generated content is correct or appropriate and must be reviewed by a human for accuracy' warns of errors and requires review, P31.
units.anchor: Not all AI generated content is correct or appropriate and must be reviewed

units.why: Use cases that do not align with University principles 'must be reviewed by IT Policy & Compliance prior to use'; a pre-use review gate, P50 (vetted tools) as nearest.
units.anchor: must be reviewed by IT Policy & Compliance prior to use.
units.frag_start: AI applications and/or the intended use case

units.why: 'AI models may be trained using underrepresented datasets creating biases' names bias as a risk, P53.
units.anchor: AI models may be trained using underrepresented datasets creating biases in the data.

units.why: 'Third parties may perform unauthorized data collection and use data inappropriately' names a data risk; privacy concern, P50.
units.anchor: Third parties may perform unauthorized data collection and use data inappropriately.

units.why: 'AI systems are a target for cyberattacks' leading to 'data breaches' names a security risk to data; P50 nearest.
units.anchor: AI systems are a target for cyberattacks due to their handling of large amounts

units.why: 'AI can be used to create realistic but fake content (deepfakes) which can be used to spread misinformation' names a harm, P53.
units.anchor: AI can be used to create realistic but fake content (deepfakes)

documents.unit: JMU Libraries (with Center for Faculty Innovation)
documents.title: Academic Integrity, Syllabi Statements and AI (Artificial Intelligence in Education guide)
documents.summary: A library research guide that advises instructors how to write syllabus statements and set AI expectations assignment by assignment using a five-level scale. It recommends against AI detectors and for process evidence. It is advice, not an enforceable policy.
documents.stance_why: The guide offers a five-level scale and says 'Choose a level for each assignment, not just the course', so it sets no stance itself and hands the decision to instructors and assignments, which makes it delegates with tiers.

units.why: The guide says clear expectations should 'truly support student learning and cognitive gain'; a rationale for clear expectations. P41 does not fit (no skill-shortcut claim), so P09's purpose is the nearest, though it is advice rather than a mandate.
units.anchor: Clear expectations in classes are supposed to truly support student learning and cognitive gain.

units.why: The guide says generative AI tools 'shouldn't replace' writing and thinking and students 'should still do substantial writing and reflection of their own'; students stay the primary thinker, P32.
units.anchor: can provide limited help with writing and thinking but shouldn't replace either

units.why: 'Faculty are encouraged to uphold a human-centered approach to feedback' is advice to instructors on their own feedback practice, P59.
units.anchor: Faculty are encouraged to uphold a human-centered approach to feedback.

units.why: Recommends 'post a clear AI policy in every course' (citing MIT's committee); a syllabus-statement expectation, P09.
units.anchor: post a clear AI policy in every course
units.frag_start: Two of its recommendations are supportive

units.why: Advises instructors to 'explain the reasoning in terms of what and how students can truly learn'; communicating the rationale to students, filed under P09 as part of the syllabus statement.
units.anchor: explain the reasoning in terms of what and how students can truly learn

units.why: The report 'also advises against relying on AI detectors' (cited by the guide), an anti-detector stance, P39.
units.anchor: The report also advises against relying on AI detectors.

units.why: 'Start with the why. Before choosing a policy, decide what students should be able to do by the end of the course' is policy-design advice to instructors; syllabus-statement preparation, P09.
units.anchor: decide what students should be able to do by the end of the course

units.why: The guide points to CMU's example policies that 'sort into no use, conditional use, and encouraged use', and Kentucky's three categories; named categories of use, P05.
units.anchor: sort into no use, conditional use, and encouraged use

units.why: 'Reuse and adapt with credit' tells instructors to adapt others' policies and credit them; advice on drafting statements, P09.
units.anchor: Reuse and adapt with credit.

units.why: Suggests 'drafting the class statement together in week one' with students; a co-created policy in the first week, P09 (communicating expectations) nearest.
units.anchor: Try drafting the class statement together in week one.

units.why: 'Students are more likely to understand a policy when they partake in the process' gives the reason for co-creation, a rationale for communicating expectations, P09.
units.anchor: Students are more likely to understand a policy when they partake in the process.

units.why: The guide recommends the Generative AI Acceptable Use Scale to 'adjust assessments' and tell 'students where AI may be used'; a named-levels scheme, P05.
units.anchor: helps instructors adjust assessments, tells students where AI may be used
units.frag_start: The Generative AI Acceptable Use Scale

units.why: Level 1, 'No AI', says students complete the work 'entirely on your own without generative AI tools'; a no-AI tier, coded P05 because it is one tier of the scale rather than a course-wide default.
units.anchor: Complete the work entirely on your own without generative AI tools.

units.why: Under Level 1 the guide suggests 'collecting rough drafts or notes' and explaining why independent practice matters; process evidence as trust-building, P35 (redesign grading/assignments) nearest.
units.anchor: Explaining why independent practice matters; collecting rough drafts or notes.

units.why: Level 2 lets students 'Brainstorm topics or outline structures; write the final content yourself'; permitted brainstorming, P15.
units.anchor: Brainstorm topics or outline structures; write the final content yourself.

units.why: Level 2 trust-builder: 'Asking for information on prompts used and why and key takeaways'; asks students to report prompts and takeaways, P26.
units.anchor: Asking for information on prompts used and why and key takeaways from the process.

units.why: Level 3 lets students 'Polish your own draft for clarity and grammar; generate no new content'; AI for prose editing, P18.
units.anchor: Polish your own draft for clarity and grammar; generate no

units.why: Level 3 trust-builder: 'Attaching the original unedited draft in an appendix'; submitting drafts as process evidence, P26.
units.anchor: Attaching the original unedited draft in an appendix.

units.why: Level 4 lets students 'Use AI for specific tasks' while they 'evaluate, critique, and fact-check all output'; permits AI use with conditions, and the verification duty is the load-bearing condition, P31.
units.anchor: Use AI for specific tasks; evaluate, critique, and fact-check all

units.why: Level 4 trust-builder: 'Requiring standard citations and a critique of the AI output'; a citation requirement for AI use, P24.
units.anchor: Requiring standard citations and a critique of the AI output.

units.why: Level 5 lets students 'Collaborate fully with AI across the project without restriction'; open permission, P02.
units.anchor: Collaborate fully with AI across the project without restriction.

units.why: Level 5 trust-builder: 'Requiring an oral discussion of the topic or assigning a reflection'; checks understanding through discussion, P34 chosen over P26 since oral discussion is named first.
units.anchor: Requiring an oral discussion of the topic or assigning

units.why: 'Choose a level for each assignment, not just the course, and note it in the syllabus and on the assignment sheet' sets the rule per assignment; P04 (assignment-level decisions) over P09 because the core is choosing per assignment.
units.anchor: Choose a level for each assignment, not just the course

units.why: 'JMU doesn't currently endorse an AI detection tool, since false positives make the results questionable' says detectors are unreliable, P39.
units.anchor: JMU doesn't currently endorse an AI detection tool, since false positives make the results questionable.

units.why: 'Lean on process instead: drafts, checkpoints, short reflections, and conversations' recommends process evidence over detection; P40 (process evidence instead) fits.
units.anchor: Lean on process instead: drafts, checkpoints, short reflections, and conversations.

units.why: 'Be explicit in your syllabus right from day one' tells instructors to state AI expectations in the syllabus at the start, P09.
units.anchor: Be explicit in your syllabus right from day one.

units.why: 'Talk through the decision-making around why GenAI is allowed or not for your class' tells instructors to explain the pedagogical rationale to students; filed under P09 as part of communicating the policy.
units.anchor: Talk through the decision-making around why GenAI is allowed or not for your class

units.why: 'Create space for conversation about the appropriateness of use of the technology' asks instructors to open dialogue so the class builds 'shared understanding about expectations'; communicating expectations, P09.
units.anchor: Create space for conversation about the appropriateness of use of the technology

notes: Coded two included university-layer documents. The IT standard is about university data and tools, so most units are privacy and tool-approval rules (P50). The DeepSeek ban is UNCOVERED (named-tool ban). Guide text cites an MIT report dated August 2026 as in source.
